Introduction to streeR

Source: vignettes/streeR-intro.Rmd
streeR-intro.Rmd

Overview

streeR fits oblique classification trees: decision trees in which each internal node splits the data using a support vector machine (SVM) hyperplane, instead of a threshold on a single variable. This lets a single node separate classes using a combination of features, which can produce much shallower and more accurate trees than an axis-parallel tree such as rpart on datasets where classes are separated by oblique boundaries.

For datasets with more than two classes, streeR uses a one-vs-rest strategy at every node: each class is tried in turn as “this class” versus “everything else”, an SVM hyperplane is fit for each candidate, and the hyperplane whose resulting split has the lowest weighted impurity (entropy or Gini) is kept. This approach, and the underlying algorithm, follows Montanana, Gamez and Puerta (2021), STree: A Single Multi-class Oblique Decision Tree Based on Support Vector Machines.

Fitting a tree 

library(streeR)

We use the classic iris dataset, which has three classes and four numeric predictors:

fit <- stree(Species ~ ., data = iris, max_depth = 3, kernel = "linear")
fit
#> STree oblique classification tree
#> Call:  stree(formula = Species ~ ., data = iris, kernel = "linear",     max_depth = 3)
#> Classes: setosa, versicolor, virginica 
#> Kernel: linear
#> 
#>  [Node] depth = 1 | n = 150 | kernel = linear | split: setosa vs rest | impurity = 0.6667
#>  |- Positive branch (distance > 0):
#> |   [Leaf] predict = setosa | n = 50
#>  `- Negative branch (distance <= 0):
#>     [Node] depth = 2 | n = 100 | kernel = linear
#>     |- Positive branch (distance > 0):
#>    |   [Leaf] predict = versicolor | n = 46
#>     `- Negative branch (distance <= 0):
#>        [Leaf] predict = virginica | n = 54

print() shows a depth-first sketch of the tree: at each internal node, the class used in that node’s one-vs-rest split (for multi-class problems) and the split’s weighted impurity; at each leaf, the predicted class and the number of training observations that reached it.

summary() gives a compact overview:

summary(fit)
#> STree oblique classification tree
#> Call:          stree(formula = Species ~ ., data = iris, kernel = "linear",     max_depth = 3)
#> Response:      Species
#> Classes:       setosa, versicolor, virginica
#> Kernel:        linear
#> Impurity used: entropy
#> Tree depth:    2 (max_depth = 3)
#> Number of leaves: 3 
#> Number of nodes: 5

Predicting

predict() returns class labels by default, or a matrix of class probabilities with type = "prob":

predict(fit, iris[1:5, ])
#> [1] setosa setosa setosa setosa setosa
#> Levels: setosa versicolor virginica
predict(fit, iris[1:5, ], type = "prob")
#>      setosa versicolor virginica
#> [1,]      1          0         0
#> [2,]      1          0         0
#> [3,]      1          0         0
#> [4,]      1          0         0
#> [5,]      1          0         0

Training accuracy on iris (for illustration only — always evaluate on held-out data in practice):

preds <- predict(fit, iris)
mean(preds == iris$Species)
#> [1] 0.9733333

Tuning

Key arguments to stree():

  • kernel: "linear", "polynomial", or "radial", passed to the underlying [e1071::svm()] call at each node.
  • max_depth / min_samples: standard tree stopping rules.
  • impurity_measure: "entropy" or "gini", used only when there are more than two classes at a node (to score the one-vs-rest candidates).
  • cost: the SVM cost/regularization parameter C.
  • scale: whether predictors are standardized before each node’s SVM is fit (recommended, and the default).
  • ...: further arguments passed to [e1071::svm()], such as gamma for a radial kernel.
fit_radial <- stree(Species ~ ., data = iris, kernel = "radial", gamma = 0.5, max_depth = 3)
summary(fit_radial)
#> STree oblique classification tree
#> Call:          stree(formula = Species ~ ., data = iris, kernel = "radial",     max_depth = 3, gamma = 0.5)
#> Response:      Species
#> Classes:       setosa, versicolor, virginica
#> Kernel:        radial
#> Impurity used: entropy
#> Tree depth:    2 (max_depth = 3)
#> Number of leaves: 3 
#> Number of nodes: 5

Reference

Montanana, R., Gamez, J. A., Puerta, J. M. (2021). STree: A Single Multi-class Oblique Decision Tree Based on Support Vector Machines. In Advances in Artificial Intelligence, LNAI 12882, Springer.
